query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small boron addition (≈3 at.% substituted for one of the transition-metal constituents) into a phosphorus-containing high-entropy / compositionally complex alloy (HEA/CCA) will raise both (i) the critical casting diameter for a fully amorphous rod and (ii) the onset temperature of crystallisation, compared with an otherwise identical baseline alloy that contains no boron.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-principal element alloy containing ≥5 transition metals (e.g. Fe, Co, Ni, Cr, Mo) and 12–20 at.% P, fully molten, cast into cylindrical rods under an inert atmosphere; no boron present.
generation.intervention: Add 3 at.% B at the expense of an equal atomic percent of the majority transition-metal element (single-step compositional substitution).
generation.conditions: Inert melting and suction-casting into rods 1–5 mm in diameter; cooling rates 10²–10³ K s⁻¹; overall P content maintained ≥12 at.%; total B kept ≤5 at.% to avoid brittle boride precipitation.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of mixed B–P–transition-metal covalent clusters that increase packing density and icosahedral short-range order, giving higher melt viscosity and greater topological frustration.
generation.mechanism: Boron, being very small and strongly covalent, (1) lowers the liquidus by creating deep eutectics with transition metals and P, thereby reducing the driving force for crystallisation, and (2) binds with P to form hetero-atomic clusters that block diffusive pathways. The combined effect suppresses crystal nucleation and growth, enhancing glass-forming ability and delaying the primary crystallisation event in the amorphous solid.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the B-free baseline alloy: • Critical fully-amorphous casting diameter increases by ≥25 % (e.g. from 2 mm to ≥2.5 mm). • Onset crystallisation temperature (Tx) in DSC rises by ≥20 °C. • Supercooled liquid region ΔTx (= Tx – Tg) widens correspondingly.
generation.baseline: Same alloy family and processing history but containing 0 at.% B (all other elements at their pre-substitution levels).
generation.boundary: The improvement should vanish or reverse if total B exceeds ~5 at.% (boride precipitation) or if P <10 at.% (insufficient P–B clustering). It is also expected to be negligible in melt-spun ribbons where cooling rates >10⁵ K s⁻¹ already overwhelm the nucleation kinetics.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the diameter and ΔTx gains is estimated; actual values could vary with exact base composition. Lack of published data on B-P synergy in HEAs means the effect could be smaller or composition-dependent.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys differing only in B content (0 at.% vs 3 at.% B, P kept constant). Arc-melt under Ar, suction-cast rods of diameters 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 mm. Characterise structure by XRD and TEM; measure Tg and Tx by DSC (20 K min⁻¹).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the 3 at.% B alloy does NOT show (a) a ≥10 % increase in critical amorphous diameter AND (b) Tx ≤ baseline Tx (i.e. no significant upward shift), the hypothesis is falsified.
